q: The Bimal Jalan Committee (2018-19) was set up to review the:

options.A: Economic Capital Framework of the Reserve Bank of India

e: The Bimal Jalan Committee (2018-19) reviewed the Economic Capital Framework of the Reserve Bank of India and recommended how much surplus the RBI should transfer to the Government.

q: The P. J. Nayak Committee (2014) is associated with:

options.C: Governance of the boards of banks in India

e: The P. J. Nayak Committee (2014) examined the governance of the boards of banks in India and recommended reducing Government holding in public sector banks.

q: The National Commission for Religious and Linguistic Minorities (2004) was chaired by:
e: The National Commission for Religious and Linguistic Minorities (2004), which examined welfare measures for minorities, was chaired by Justice Ranganath Misra, former Chief Justice of India.

q: Bandipur National Park, famous for its tigers and elephants, is located in the State of:
e: Bandipur National Park, a Project Tiger reserve famous for tigers, elephants and gaurs in the Nilgiri landscape, is located in Karnataka.

q: The Athirappilly Falls, among the largest waterfalls of India, are located in the State of:
e: The Athirappilly Falls, often called the Niagara of India and among the largest waterfalls of the country, are on the Chalakudy river in Kerala.

q: The Koyna Dam, one of the largest dams of its State, is located in:
e: The Koyna Dam, built across the Koyna river and known for the Koyna hydroelectric project, is located in the Satara district of Maharashtra.

q: Doddabetta, the highest peak of the Nilgiri Hills, is located in the State of:
e: Doddabetta, at about 2,637 metres the highest peak of the Nilgiri Hills, is located near Udhagamandalam (Ooty) in Tamil Nadu.

q: The Zoji La pass connects the Kashmir Valley with:
e: The Zoji La pass, on the Srinagar-Leh highway, connects the Kashmir Valley with Ladakh across the Great Himalayan range.

q: Pangong Tso, the famous high-altitude lake, is located in:
e: Pangong Tso, the high-altitude lake about 134 km long extending from India into Tibet, is located in Ladakh.

q: The capital of Mizoram is:
e: Aizawl is the capital of Mizoram, the hill city in the north-east that is also the State's largest urban centre.

q: The Mahanadi river originates in the State of:
e: The Mahanadi river originates from the Sihawa hills near Raipur in Chhattisgarh and flows east through Odisha to the Bay of Bengal.

q: The rock-cut Kailasa Temple at Ellora was built under the patronage of the Rashtrakuta ruler:
e: The rock-cut Kailasa Temple at Ellora, carved top-down from a single rock, was built under the patronage of the Rashtrakuta ruler Krishna I in the 8th century.

q: Mahatma Gandhi was assassinated in 1948 by:
e: Mahatma Gandhi was assassinated on 30 January 1948 at Birla House, New Delhi, by Nathuram Godse.

q: The modern ballpoint pen was invented by:
e: The modern ballpoint pen, using a small rotating ball to dispense quick-drying ink, was patented and popularised by the Hungarian journalist Laszlo Biro.

q: A galvanometer is an instrument used to:

options.B: Measure the depth of the ocean
options.C: Detect and measure small electric currents

e: A galvanometer is a sensitive instrument used to detect and measure small electric currents by the deflection of a needle in a magnetic field.

q: The chemical name of common salt is:
e: Common salt is sodium chloride, a compound of sodium and chlorine with the chemical formula NaCl.

q: The Nobel Prizes are presented every year on:
e: The Nobel Prizes are presented every year on 10 December, the anniversary of the death of Alfred Nobel, in Stockholm and Oslo.

q: The Commonwealth Games of 2010 were hosted by the city of:
e: The Commonwealth Games of 2010 were hosted by New Delhi, India, at venues including the Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium.

q: Bharatanatyam is the classical dance form of the State of:
e: Bharatanatyam, one of the oldest classical dance forms of India, originating in the temples of its home State, belongs to Tamil Nadu.

q: Onam, the harvest festival celebrated with boat races and floral carpets, belongs to the State of:
e: Onam, the harvest festival marked by pookkalam floral carpets, sadhya feasts and vallamkali boat races, is the State festival of Kerala.

q: Rail Vikas Nigam Limited (RVNL) was granted the 'Navratna' status by the Government of India in the year:
e: Rail Vikas Nigam Limited (RVNL) was granted Navratna status by the Government of India in 2023, after its listing and strong project performance.

q: RITES Limited, the engineering and consultancy organisation of the Ministry of Railways, was incorporated in the year:
e: RITES Limited, the transport infrastructure consultancy and engineering PSU of the Ministry of Railways, was incorporated in 1974.

q: IRCON International Limited, the construction organisation of the Ministry of Railways, was incorporated in the year:
e: IRCON International Limited, the railway construction PSU that executes turnkey rail projects in India and abroad, was incorporated in 1976.

q: RailTel Corporation of India Limited was incorporated in the year:
e: RailTel Corporation of India Limited, which provides broadband and telecom services using railway right of way, was incorporated in 2000.

q: The Centre for Railway Information Systems (CRIS) was set up in the year:
e: The Centre for Railway Information Systems (CRIS), the IT arm of Indian Railways that runs systems like PRS and FOIS, was set up in 1986.

q: The Rail Land Development Authority (RLDA) was set up as a statutory authority under the:
e: The Rail Land Development Authority (RLDA) was set up as a statutory authority through the Railways (Amendment) Act, 2005, to develop vacant railway land for commercial use.

q: The Container Corporation of India Limited (CONCOR) commenced its operations in November 1989 by taking over from Indian Railways an existing network of how many inland container depots?
e: CONCOR commenced operations in November 1989 by taking over from Indian Railways an existing network of seven inland container depots (ICDs).

q: The e-catering service of IRCTC, through which passengers can order food for delivery at their seat, is provided through the mobile application named:
e: Food on Track is the IRCTC e-catering mobile application through which passengers order food online for delivery at their seat during the journey.

q: The National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited (NHSRCL) was incorporated in the year:
e: The National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited (NHSRCL), the implementing agency for the Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train corridor, was incorporated in 2016.

q: The Research Designs and Standards Organisation (RDSO) came into being in the year 1957 by integrating the Central Standards Office with the:

options.B: Indian Railways Institute of Civil Engineering

e: RDSO came into being in 1957 at Lucknow by integrating the Central Standards Office with the Railway Testing and Research Centre.

q: After the restructuring of the Railway Board in 2020, besides the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, the Board consists of how many Members?
e: After the Railway Board restructuring of 2020, besides the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, the Board consists of four Members, covering infrastructure, operations, finance and rolling stock areas.

q: Recruitment to non-gazetted posts on Indian Railways is conducted through Railway Recruitment Boards. The total number of Railway Recruitment Boards in India is:
e: There are 21 Railway Recruitment Boards in India, which conduct recruitment to non-gazetted (Group C) posts of the Indian Railways.

q: The Indian Railway Welfare Organisation (IRWO), a registered society under the Ministry of Railways, is mainly engaged in:

options.A: Running railway hospitals and health units
options.B: Promoting housing schemes for serving and retired railway employees

e: The Indian Railway Welfare Organisation (IRWO), a registered society under the Ministry of Railways, is mainly engaged in promoting housing schemes for serving and retired railway employees.

q: The North Western Railway, with headquarters at Jaipur, became operational in the year:
e: North Western Railway, headquartered at Jaipur, became operational on 1 October 2002, covering routes across Rajasthan and adjoining areas.

q: The Northeast Frontier Railway was created in 1958 by carving out the north-eastern region from the:
e: Northeast Frontier Railway was created in 1958 by carving out the north-eastern region, comprising the Pandu region, from the North Eastern Railway.

q: The South East Central Railway, which came into existence in April 2003, was carved out mainly from the:
e: South East Central Railway, headquartered at Bilaspur and formed in April 2003, was carved out mainly from the South Eastern Railway.

q: The Coach Rehabilitation Workshop (CRWS) at Nishatpura, Bhopal, under the West Central Railway, is mainly engaged in:

options.B: Periodic overhaul of freight wagons only

e: The Coach Rehabilitation Workshop (CRWS) at Nishatpura, Bhopal, under West Central Railway, mainly carries out mid-life rehabilitation of passenger coaches.

q: The Carriage Repair Workshop at Harnaut in Bihar, which undertakes periodic overhauling of passenger coaches, functions under the:
e: The Carriage Repair Workshop at Harnaut in Bihar, which does periodic overhaul of passenger coaches, functions under East Central Railway, headquartered at Hajipur.

q: The Matunga Carriage and Wagon Workshop, located in Mumbai, belongs to which zonal railway?
e: The Matunga Carriage and Wagon Workshop in Mumbai, which overhauls suburban and mainline coaches, belongs to Central Railway.

q: The Carriage and Wagon Workshop at New Bongaigaon of the Northeast Frontier Railway is located in the State of:
e: The Carriage and Wagon Workshop at New Bongaigaon of Northeast Frontier Railway is located in the State of Assam.

q: The Western Railway, formed by merging the Bombay, Baroda and Central India Railway with other State railways, was created in the year:
e: Western Railway was created on 5 November 1951 by merging the Bombay, Baroda and Central India Railway with the Saurashtra, Rajputana and Jaipur State railways.

q: The Carriage and Wagon Works at Perambur, Chennai, functions under which zonal railway?
e: The Carriage and Wagon Works at Perambur, Chennai, which builds and overhauls coaches, functions under Southern Railway.

q: The Konkan Railway system, connecting Roha in Maharashtra with Thokur in Karnataka, became fully operational in the year:
e: The Konkan Railway, running from Roha in Maharashtra to Thokur near Mangaluru in Karnataka along the west coast, became fully operational in 1998.

q: The Engineering Workshop at Sini, under the Chakradharpur division, belongs to which zonal railway?
e: The Engineering Workshop at Sini, in the Chakradharpur division, belongs to South Eastern Railway, headquartered at Garden Reach, Kolkata.

q: In railway contracts, the abbreviation 'EMD', deposited by bidders along with their tenders, stands for:
e: EMD stands for Earnest Money Deposit, the amount deposited by bidders along with their tenders as security of their earnestness to take up the contract.

q: In the National Pension System, the abbreviation 'PRAN', allotted to each subscriber, stands for:
e: In the National Pension System, PRAN stands for Permanent Retirement Account Number, the unique number allotted to each subscriber and portable across jobs and locations.

q: In railway establishment matters, the abbreviation 'SBF', a fund used for the welfare of railway staff, stands for:
e: SBF stands for Staff Benefit Fund, the fund maintained on the Railways for the welfare of railway staff and their families, including scholarships and relief.

q: In the context of annual bonus paid to railway employees, the abbreviation 'PLB' stands for:
e: PLB stands for Productivity Linked Bonus, the bonus paid annually to eligible railway employees linked to the productivity of the Railways.

q: In railway establishment rules, the leave denoted by 'CCL', admissible to women employees for taking care of their children, stands for:
e: CCL stands for Child Care Leave, admissible to women employees for taking care of their children, for a maximum of two years (730 days) during their service.

q: In railway establishment rules, the advance denoted by 'HBA', granted to an employee for building or buying a house, stands for:
e: HBA stands for House Building Advance, the advance granted to a Government or railway employee for building, buying or enlarging a house.

q: In railway commercial working, the abbreviation 'YTSK', denoting the licensed agents who sell railway tickets outside station premises, stands for:
e: YTSK stands for Yatri Ticket Suvidha Kendra, the licensed agents authorised by Indian Railways to sell reserved and unreserved tickets from premises outside railway stations.

q: In railway establishment rules, the scheme denoted by 'MACP', which provides financial upgradation to employees on completion of specified years of service, stands for:
e: MACP stands for Modified Assured Career Progression, the scheme giving financial upgradation to Central Government employees after 10, 20 and 30 years of service when regular promotion is not available.

q: In the context of group insurance for railway employees, the abbreviation 'CGEGIS' stands for:

options.A: Central Government Employees Group Insurance Scheme
options.B: Central Government Employees Gratuity Insurance Scheme
options.C: Central Government Employees General Insurance Scheme
options.D: Central Government Employees Group Investment Scheme

e: CGEGIS stands for Central Government Employees Group Insurance Scheme, the group insurance scheme introduced in 1982 for Central Government employees, including railway employees.

q: In railway establishment rules, the facility denoted by 'LTC', under which an employee can travel to a declared place during leave, stands for:
e: LTC stands for Leave Travel Concession, the concession allowing an employee to travel to the declared hometown or any place in India during leave, subject to the rules in force.

q: In management accounting and budgeting, the technique denoted by 'ZBB', under which every expense is justified afresh for each period, stands for:
e: ZBB stands for Zero Based Budgeting, a budgeting technique in which every item of expenditure is justified afresh for each new period instead of being based on the previous budget.

q: The first 'Namo Bharat Rapid Rail' service of Indian Railways, flagged off in September 2024 and earlier known as the Vande Metro, was introduced between:
e: The first Namo Bharat Rapid Rail, earlier called Vande Metro, was flagged off in September 2024 between Ahmedabad and Bhuj in Gujarat for short-distance intercity travel.

q: The successful head-on collision trial of the 'Kavach' train protection system, conducted in March 2022 between Gullaguda and Chitgidda stations, was carried out on the:
e: The March 2022 head-on collision trial of Kavach between Gullaguda and Chitgidda stations was conducted on the South Central Railway, where the indigenous system was first developed and tested.

q: 'Mission Raftaar', announced in the Railway Budget 2016-17 for increasing the speed of trains, primarily targeted:

options.A: Introduction of bullet trains on all routes
options.B: Doubling the number of freight trains
options.C: Increasing the speed of suburban trains only
options.D: Doubling the average speed of freight trains and increasing the average speed of passenger trains by 25 kmph

e: Mission Raftaar, announced in the Railway Budget 2016-17, aimed to double the average speed of freight trains and raise the average speed of passenger trains by 25 kmph.

q: The Gati Shakti Multi-Modal Cargo Terminal (GCT) policy, introduced by Indian Railways in 2021, mainly facilitates:

options.B: Development of cargo terminals on railway and non-railway land with private participation
options.C: Manufacture of freight wagons in private factories
options.D: Leasing of railway land for housing colonies

e: The Gati Shakti Multi-Modal Cargo Terminal policy of 2021 facilitates development of cargo terminals on railway and non-railway land with private participation to boost rail freight share.

q: The first-ever freight train to reach the Kashmir Valley, which arrived in August 2025 carrying cement from Rupnagar in Punjab, terminated at the:
e: In August 2025 the first freight train to the Kashmir Valley, carrying 21 wagons of cement from Rupnagar in Punjab, terminated at the newly commissioned Anantnag Goods Shed.

q: India's first Vande Bharat Sleeper train, flagged off in January 2026, was introduced on the route between:
e: India's first Vande Bharat Sleeper train was flagged off on 17 January 2026 between Howrah and Kamakhya, introducing sleeper coaches in the Vande Bharat series for overnight travel.

q: The 'Bharat Gaurav' scheme of Indian Railways, under which theme-based tourist trains are run by private tour operators and service providers, was launched in the year:
e: The Bharat Gaurav scheme was launched in 2021 to let private tour operators and service providers run theme-based tourist trains showcasing India's cultural heritage and tourist places.

q: The first 20-coach Vande Bharat Express of Indian Railways, flagged off in September 2024, was introduced between:
e: The first 20-coach Vande Bharat Express was flagged off in September 2024 between Varanasi and New Delhi, increasing capacity on the busy route with a longer rake.

q: The first State in India to achieve 100 per cent electrification of its entire broad gauge railway network was:
e: Haryana was the first State to achieve 100 per cent electrification of its entire broad gauge network, completing electrification of its 1,701 route km in March 2023.

q: The 'Kavach' automatic train protection system was commissioned in March 2026 on the Prayagraj-Kanpur section, which forms a part of the:
e: Kavach was commissioned in March 2026 on the 190 route km Prayagraj-Kanpur section, which lies on the Delhi-Howrah high-density corridor, paving the way for 160 kmph operations.

q: The novel 'Kanthapura', depicting the impact of the freedom movement on a South Indian village, was written by:
e: Kanthapura, published in 1938 and narrating the freedom movement's impact on a South Indian village through the voice of an old woman, was written by Raja Rao.

q: The novel 'A Fine Balance', set in India during the Emergency, was written by:
e: A Fine Balance, set in India during the Emergency of 1975-77 and following four characters in a city flat, was written by the Canada-based author Rohinton Mistry.

q: The novel 'The Namesake', about a Bengali immigrant family in America, was written by:
e: The Namesake, about Gogol Ganguli and his Bengali immigrant family in America, was the first novel of Jhumpa Lahiri, author of the Pulitzer-winning Interpreter of Maladies.

q: The novel 'Sea of Poppies', the first part of the Ibis trilogy, was written by:
e: Sea of Poppies, set against the opium trade and the ship Ibis, is the first volume of the Ibis trilogy written by Amitav Ghosh, followed by River of Smoke and Flood of Fire.

q: The science-fiction novel 'The Time Machine' was written by:
e: The Time Machine, the 1895 science-fiction novella about a traveller visiting the distant future of the Eloi and Morlocks, was written by H. G. Wells.

q: The play 'The Merchant of Venice' was written by:
e: The Merchant of Venice, the comedy featuring Shylock, Portia and the pound-of-flesh bond, was written by William Shakespeare.

q: The epic poem 'Paradise Lost' was written by:
e: Paradise Lost, the epic poem retelling the Fall of Man and Satan's rebellion, was written by the blind English poet John Milton and published in 1667.

q: 'The Canterbury Tales', a collection of stories told by pilgrims, was written by:
e: The Canterbury Tales, a collection of stories told by pilgrims travelling to Canterbury, was written by Geoffrey Chaucer, regarded as the father of English literature.

q: The French novel 'Madame Bovary' was written by:
e: Madame Bovary, the French realist novel about Emma Bovary's unhappy life in provincial France, was written by Gustave Flaubert and published in 1857.

q: The Russian novel 'Anna Karenina' was written by:
e: Anna Karenina, the Russian novel tracing Anna's tragic affair alongside Levin's search for meaning, was written by Leo Tolstoy, also the author of War and Peace.

q: The novel 'Oliver Twist', about an orphan boy in London, was written by:
e: Oliver Twist, about the orphan Oliver in a London workhouse and Fagin's gang, was written by Charles Dickens and published in 1838.

q: The novel 'The Adventures of Tom Sawyer' was written by:
e: The Adventures of Tom Sawyer, set on the Mississippi River and featuring Tom, Huckleberry Finn and Becky Thatcher, was written by Mark Twain, pen name of Samuel Clemens.

q: The book 'Glimpses of World History', written in the form of letters from prison, was authored by:
e: Glimpses of World History, a survey of world history written as letters to his daughter Indira from prison in 1930-33, was authored by Jawaharlal Nehru.

q: The novel 'Coolie', about the exploitation of a poor hill boy, was written by:
e: Coolie, depicting the exploitation of the hill boy Munoo as he moves through jobs and cities, was written by Mulk Raj Anand, also the author of Untouchable.

q: The novel 'A House for Mr Biswas', which won wide acclaim for its author, was written by:
e: A House for Mr Biswas, about Mohun Biswas's lifelong struggle for a house of his own in Trinidad, was written by V. S. Naipaul, later a Nobel laureate in Literature.

q: The book 'Development as Freedom' was written by the economist:
e: Development as Freedom, arguing that development means expanding the real freedoms and capabilities people enjoy, was written by the economist Amartya Sen.

q: The novel 'The English Teacher', set in the fictional town of Malgudi, was written by:
e: The English Teacher, set in R. K. Narayan's fictional town of Malgudi and centred on the schoolteacher Krishna, was written by R. K. Narayan himself.

q: The National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution (2000) was chaired by:
e: The National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution, set up in 2000, was chaired by Justice M. N. Venkatachaliah, former Chief Justice of India.

q: The Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998) is associated with recommendations on:
e: The Indrajit Gupta Committee of 1998 recommended State funding of elections to reduce the influence of money power and to create a fairer electoral process.

q: The Malimath Committee (2000-03) recommended reforms in the:
e: The Malimath Committee, chaired by Justice V. S. Malimath in 2000-03, recommended wide-ranging reforms in the criminal justice system, including investigation and trial procedures.

q: The Fifteenth Finance Commission of India was chaired by:
e: The Fifteenth Finance Commission, which recommended tax devolution for 2021-26, was chaired by N. K. Singh, former Revenue Secretary and Rajya Sabha member.

q: The Committee on Financial Sector Reforms (2008), which gave the report 'A Hundred Small Steps', was chaired by:
e: The Committee on Financial Sector Reforms of 2008, whose report was titled A Hundred Small Steps, was chaired by Raghuram Rajan, later Governor of the Reserve Bank of India.

q: The Expert Group set up in 2012 to review the methodology for the measurement of poverty was chaired by:
e: The Expert Group set up in 2012 to review the methodology for measurement of poverty was chaired by C. Rangarajan, whose report revised the official poverty estimates.

q: The Bezbaruah Committee (2014) was set up to look into the concerns of the people of:

options.B: The North-Eastern region living in other parts of India

e: The Bezbaruah Committee of 2014, chaired by M. P. Bezbaruah, looked into the concerns of people from the North-Eastern region living in other parts of India, especially their safety.

q: The Yash Pal Committee (2009) submitted its report on the renovation and rejuvenation of:
e: The Yash Pal Committee of 2009 submitted its report on the renovation and rejuvenation of higher education, recommending a single national commission for the sector.

q: The SEBI Committee on Corporate Governance (2017) was chaired by:
e: The SEBI Committee on Corporate Governance of 2017, which recommended stronger board and disclosure norms for listed companies, was chaired by Uday Kotak.

q: The High-Powered Committee (2007) on making Mumbai an International Financial Centre was chaired by:
e: The High-Powered Committee of 2007 on making Mumbai an International Financial Centre was chaired by Percy Mistry, and is commonly called the Percy Mistry Committee.

q: The committee that submitted the draft National Education Policy in 2019 was chaired by:
e: The committee that submitted the draft National Education Policy in 2019 was chaired by Dr. K. Kasturirangan, former Chairman of ISRO.

q: Kuchipudi is a classical dance form of the State of:
e: Kuchipudi, originating in the village of Kuchipudi with dance-drama performances based on the Ramayana and Mahabharata, is the classical dance form of Andhra Pradesh.

q: Mohiniyattam is a classical dance form of the State of:
e: Mohiniyattam, the graceful solo dance of the enchantress Mohini performed mainly by women, is the classical dance form of Kerala.

q: Pongal, the harvest festival celebrated in the month of January, is the major festival of:
e: Pongal, the four-day harvest festival thanking the Sun God for the rice harvest and celebrated in mid-January, is the major festival of Tamil Nadu.

q: Bihu is the principal festival of the State of:
e: Bihu, celebrated as Rongali, Kongali and Bhogali Bihu through the year to mark the Assamese New Year and the agricultural cycle, is the principal festival of Assam.

q: The Hornbill Festival, named after a bird and showcasing Naga culture, is celebrated in:
e: The Hornbill Festival, held every December at Kisama near Kohima and named after the hornbill bird, showcases the culture of the Naga tribes of Nagaland.

q: The Gateway of India, built to commemorate the visit of King George V, is located in:
e: The Gateway of India, the basalt arch in Mumbai built to commemorate the landing of King George V and Queen Mary in 1911, stands at Apollo Bunder overlooking the Arabian Sea.

q: The construction of the Qutub Minar at Delhi was begun by:
e: Construction of the Qutub Minar at Delhi was begun by Qutb-ud-din Aibak, founder of the Slave dynasty, and was later completed by Iltutmish.
